name: Simon
overview: Simon, also known as Peter, is a male disciple of YHVH distinguished as the brother of Andrew and a fisherman by trade. He is one of the Twelve Apostles and carries the surname Barjona, indicating his lineage as the son of Jonah. Simon hails from the city of Bethsaida, marking his geographical and cultural background within the Gospel narrative.
namesAndTitles: The name Simon means 'he has heard' or 'obedient one,' reflecting a personal identity grounded in responsiveness. God bestowed upon him the name Peter, meaning 'rock,' signifying his foundational role among the disciples. He is also called Simon Barjona, meaning 'son of Jonah,' and Cephas, another term meaning 'rock,' underscoring his significance in the early church.
familyAndRelationships: Simon is noted explicitly as the brother of Andrew, establishing a familial link within the circle of Jesus' followers. He is a disciple and apostle of YHVH, affirming his committed role in Christ's ministry. Additionally, he is identified as the son of Jonah, providing a paternal connection mentioned in Scripture.
scriptureSignificance: Simon Peter is a central figure among Jesus' Twelve Apostles, recognized for his close relationship with Christ and his leadership role. His background as a fisherman from Bethsaida highlights his humble origins before being called to discipleship. The conferral of the name Peter by Jesus signifies his destined role as a 'rock' in the foundation of the church, marking him as a pivotal character in the Gospel accounts.
